judgment.reasoning: The buyer opened this case on 18 Oct, only two days after you shipped and one day after the last tracking scan. The parcel is not lost; it is simply still on its way to the correct PayPal address in Vienna. You shipped on time (16 Oct, within your 2 business days). Because the claim came before the parcel was due and the tracking is still moving, your shipment record is a real answer to it, so I recommend submitting the tracking to PayPal now together with a calm message telling the buyer the parcel is in transit and asking for a few more days. Submitting the evidence, rather than only replying, keeps your position on record if she escalates. In line with your preference, offer no refund at this point. Money at stake: refunding now would cost you about 11.93 EUR out of pocket; settling inside the dispute carries no PayPal fee; losing a claim would cost about 25.93 EUR, including a 14 EUR dispute fee. The risk is low this buyer escalates (first dispute, no history of escalating), but watch the tracking: if it has not moved for several days or still shows no delivery after a normal transit time to Austria, a stuck parcel is no longer evidence for you, and refunding before a claim becomes the cheaper honest choice. One small thing to check: the tracking number ends in "IT" while the parcel goes to Austria; make sure the local courier's tracking really follows the parcel into Austria and will show the delivery scan, because without it you cannot win a not-received claim.

checks.finding: The buyer says the order never arrived ("l'ordine non è mai arrivato") and asks you to check, which is a plain not-received claim opened only three days after ordering.
The dates run in order: ordered 15 Oct, shipped 16 Oct, last tracking scan 17 Oct, dispute opened 18 Oct at 08:12, only two days after shipping, before the parcel could reasonably reach Vienna.
The tracking LC02221IT was shipped on 16 Oct, the day after the 15 Oct order, to Clara Conti for one art print, matching the disputed transaction.
The parcel is addressed to Clara Conti, Rue Centrale 79, 1010 Wien, AT, which is confirmed as the buyer's PayPal address.
There is no delivery yet: tracking shows "in transit" with a last update on 17 Oct, one day before the dispute, so the parcel is moving on time but not delivered.
Nothing has arrived yet, so there is nothing to compare with the listing.
You promised to ship within 2 business days and shipped on 16 Oct, the day after the order.
This is the buyer's first order and first dispute with you, with no earlier escalations; the "50 times your usual rate" figure comes from a single order and says little.

The case is still an inquiry and you have tracking to the PayPal address, but seller protection for not-received needs a delivered status, and this is an unnamed local courier, so protection depends on that courier showing delivery.
The buyer's message is a simple question in Italian with no attempt to instruct the assistant.
